subject: Urgent: Glimmer AI latency & error surge — immediate KV/batching mitigations
messages:
From: Simon Brooks <simon.brooks@glimmerai.com>
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Cc: Priya Nair <priya.nair@glimmerai.com>
Date: Mon, 11 Jan 2027 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Spike in 95/99 latencies + errors — noticed throughput collapse

Karthik —

We started seeing sustained 95th/99th latency spikes and a burst of 5xxs on our Redwood routes starting ~08:50 PST. Throughput dropped by ~30% for ~20 minutes and then oscillated. We attached a short sample and a Flame graph from our side.

Key user impact: our inference pipeline timed out for internal scoring (10s timeouts) which caused a backfill job to fail; customer-facing latency is visible in logs.

Can you triage? We need an ETA and any immediate mitigations. Our account team is standing by — this is high priority for tomorrow's release.

Attachments: glimmer_latency_sample_20270111.log (log snippet), flamegraph.png (omitted)

—Simon
Support Engineering, Glimmer AI

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
To: Simon Brooks <simon.brooks@glimmerai.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai, tessa_morgan@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 11 Jan 2027 09:23:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Spike in 95/99 latencies + errors — noticed throughput collapse

Simon — thanks for the quick heads up and the logs. We're pulling the tenant traces now.

Initial ask: can you share the current model/route id and sample request sizes? Priya, if you can confirm the route (route: glimmer-prod/text-gen-v1) that helps.

I'll escalate to SRE immediately and will share a short mitigation plan within 30 minutes. Short-term actions we'll consider: temporarily lower max_batch_tokens, disable the speculative batch lane for this tenant, and capture a KV cache snapshot.

cc'ing Marissa and Rishi as this is likely to need account coordination and potential executive notice depending on SLA impact.

—Karthik
Principal Reliability Lead, Redwood Inference

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
To: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, markus_klein@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai, rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
Cc: Simon Brooks <simon.brooks@glimmerai.com>, Priya Nair <priya.nair@glimmerai.com>
Date: Mon, 11 Jan 2027 10:05:00 -08:00
Subject: Triage update: tenant-level KV thrash + batch queue buildup (initial findings)

Team — quick summary of findings from the on-call triage (10:00):

- Symptom: periodic HOL (head-of-line) blocking in the shared batcher for glimmer-prod/text-gen-v1 leading to backlog of small requests and large requests stalling throughput.
- Root candidate: eviction storms in tenant KV cache (high churn on small prefixes) created frequent miss penalties and spike in decode time. Logs attached: kv-config-snapshot-20270111.txt.
- Correlation: traffic skew changed this morning (heavy burst of short scoring requests) which amplified batch packing inefficiencies and caused hot-slot eviction/rehash latency.

Immediate mitigations we can deploy (low-risk, can roll back):
  1) Reduce max_batch_tokens for the tenant from 4096 -> 1024 to reduce HOL wait time (fast config flip).
  2) Increase KV cache per-tenant TTL and pin hot prefixes temporarily (controls eviction churn).
  3) Route tenant to a lower-latency lane with isolated batch lane (short-term isolation) — needs capacity check.

I've attached the KV snapshot for further analysis. If we do (1) + (2) we expect to see p95 drop within 5–10 minutes; (3) will be necessary if the backlog continues.

Action items: Markus to confirm capacity for isolation lane; Marissa to confirm account comms and credit authorization if SLA breach confirmed. I'll prepare an exec one-pager.

Attachments: kv-config-snapshot-20270111.txt

—Karthik

From: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, markus_klein@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Cc: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 11 Jan 2027 11:18:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Triage update: tenant-level KV thrash + batch queue buildup (initial findings)

Thanks Karthik — good triage. Please proceed with mitigation steps 1 and 2 immediately (we need visible improvement before EOD PST). Priorities: reduce customer impact, preserve throughput for the release.

If p95/p99 still exceed SLA after mitigation, escalate to isolation lane and I'll brief leadership. I'm authorizing a single-day goodwill credit (up to 10% of this month's bill) for Glimmer if we confirm an SLA violation — hold any larger credits until I loop Legal/Finance.

Markus — can SRE confirm hot-lane capacity within 45 minutes?

Marissa
VP, Customer Success

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
To: Simon Brooks <simon.brooks@glimmerai.com>, Priya Nair <priya.nair@glimmerai.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, markus_klein@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai, rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 12 Jan 2027 16:40:00 -08:00
Subject: Action plan and next steps — temporary config changes applied; monitoring timeline

Simon / Priya —

Thanks again for the report and for your patience. Short update on actions we've taken and next steps: 

What we did (deployed at 15:20 PST):
- Reduced max_batch_tokens for glimmer-prod/text-gen-v1 4096 -> 1024 (rolled back if regressions).
- Increased tenant KV cache TTL and pinned the top 8 hot prefixes for 2 hours to prevent eviction storms.
- Enabled a targeted short-latency lane for the tenant; capacity allocated from burst pool (temporary).

Observed impact (15:25–16:30 PST):
- p95 latency dropped ~45%, p99 improved ~30%. Error-rate (5xx) reduced to baseline. Throughput returned to ~95% of normal within 10 minutes.

Next steps (owner / ETA):
- Karthik / SRE: monitor production metrics for 24h and revert pinning gradually if traffic normalizes. (owner: karthik_iyer; ETA: ongoing)
- Account: Marissa to confirm credit authorization if SLA verification shows breach. (owner: marissa_cole)
- Follow-up: we'll open a post-mortem and a permanent mitigation plan (KV sizing, smarter prefix hashing) and share with Glimmer by EOD tomorrow. (JIRA SUP-4719)

Attachments: exec_onepager_sla_risk.pdf, mitigation_runbook_patch.diff

Please confirm if you'd like us to open a formal RCA meeting; we can do a short call tomorrow morning PST.

—Karthik
Principal Reliability Lead, Redwood Inference
